note: Vessel waypoints for sweeps_soft.py (format: its docstring). Anatomy is data: each entry cites its sources and says what is derived and what is schematic. Written by CP-1+ (first pass, to be vetted): every course between waypoints is a straight chart segment, every point is `inferred`, and the radii are stated defaults.

s.anterior-ethmoidal-septal-branch.L.variable: Entry depends on the turbinate's axilla, which the specimen approximates with the turbinate head.
s.anterior-ethmoidal-septal-branch.L.derivation: Entry: 7.35 mm behind the septal projection of the middle turbinate head (Gras-Cabrerizo 2016, mean of 10 cavities), near the top of the septum. Descent is a schematic line; the paper gives the entry, not the course.

s.anterior-ethmoidal-septal-branch.R.variable: Entry depends on the turbinate's axilla, which the specimen approximates with the turbinate head.
s.anterior-ethmoidal-septal-branch.R.derivation: Entry: 7.35 mm behind the septal projection of the middle turbinate head (Gras-Cabrerizo 2016, mean of 10 cavities), near the top of the septum. Descent is a schematic line; the paper gives the entry, not the course.

s.nasopalatine-artery.L.variable: The incisive-canal end is derived from a mean (39.6 ± 4.3 mm) measured on sagittal CT in 9 heads.
s.nasopalatine-artery.L.derivation: End at the incisive canal, placed 39.6 mm in front of the choanal arch level (Bleier 2011: the flap length from the incisive canal to the sphenoid face at the choanal arch), i.e. A -11.9, near the septal chart's floor edge (the chart's lower edge rises toward the nose, so the end sits a few mm above the floor line). The canal itself is not resolved in the specimen. The start continues the inferior branch.

s.nasopalatine-artery.R.variable: The incisive-canal end is derived from a mean (39.6 ± 4.3 mm) measured on sagittal CT in 9 heads.
s.nasopalatine-artery.R.derivation: End at the incisive canal, placed 39.6 mm in front of the choanal arch level (Bleier 2011: the flap length from the incisive canal to the sphenoid face at the choanal arch), i.e. A -11.9, near the septal chart's floor edge (the chart's lower edge rises toward the nose, so the end sits a few mm above the floor line). The canal itself is not resolved in the specimen. The start continues the inferior branch.

s.posterior-septal-artery-inferior-branc.variable: Which branch is dominant, and where the artery divides, vary between sides and people (Zhang 2014: dominant inferior in 61.5%, division near the sphenopalatine foramen in 65.4%).
s.posterior-septal-artery-inferior-branc.derivation: Start: the middle of the strip between the choanal arch (S 12.0) and the sphenoid ostium on the chart's posterior edge (the specimen's septal surface ends about 4 mm in front of the rostrum). Course: down the posterior border, then anteroinferiorly (Zhang 2014); the straight chart segments between waypoints are schematic, not observed. On the left the septal surface starts 3 mm further forward at this height (A -43), so the start is moved there.

s.posterior-septal-artery-inferior-branc.variable: Which branch is dominant, and where the artery divides, vary between sides and people (Zhang 2014: dominant inferior in 61.5%, division near the sphenopalatine foramen in 65.4%).
s.posterior-septal-artery-inferior-branc.derivation: Start: the middle of the strip between the choanal arch (S 12.0) and the sphenoid ostium on the chart's posterior edge (the specimen's septal surface ends about 4 mm in front of the rostrum). Course: down the posterior border, then anteroinferiorly (Zhang 2014); the straight chart segments between waypoints are schematic, not observed. On the right a gap in the septal surface at A -46, S 14-15 forces the start 2 mm forward (A -44).

s.posterior-septal-artery-superior-branc.variable: Course of the superior branch is not described in the sources read for this pass; it is drawn short, toward the upper septum.
s.posterior-septal-artery-superior-branc.derivation: Start as the inferior branch. The direction (forward and up along the upper septum, ending about 10 mm below its top) is schematic and has no cited waypoint; verify before relying on it. On the left the septal surface starts 3 mm further forward at this height (A -43), so the start is moved there.

s.posterior-septal-artery-superior-branc.derivation: Start as the inferior branch. On the right a gap in the septal surface at A -46, S 14-15 forces the start 2 mm forward (A -44).

s.superior-labial-septal-branch.L.variable: Entry level at the columella varies; the specimen's face mask removed the entry.
s.superior-labial-septal-branch.L.derivation: Truncated: the artery enters at the columella and caudal septum, which the specimen's mask removed, so only an ascending segment along the anterior septal margin is drawn from the first on-chart point.
